headings.title: SMTO-GWT-0039 — This computer can't do that kind of work as asked

html:
SMTO-GWT-0039 — This computer can't do that kind of work as asked

GUID: 51a05d05-a2bb-4749-b530-fa9512338d35
Slug: gateway-capability-unsupported
Domain: GWT · Subsystem: gwt

What happened

  • The Gateway on the chosen computer couldn't handle this request, for example running something with administrator rights, opening a live terminal, or a particular file action. Usually its Gateway is out of date or doesn't offer that feature.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Settings › Setup › Gateways, expand the computer, and under Software updates select Check for updates. Install any update offered. Older Gateways lack some features SMTO now asks for, such as administrator commands or newer file actions.
  2. Check whether what you asked for already happened on that computer, for example whether the file changed, before asking again. SMTO stopped at this step, but earlier steps of the Task may already have run.
  3. If the message mentions terminal sessions on a Windows computer, ask SMTO in a new message to run the command without a live terminal. That Windows setup can run commands, but can't keep a live terminal window open.
  4. If it still can't do it, select a different computer with the Target button below the message box and send the request again. Another computer's Gateway may already support this feature.

What success looks like

  • The request runs on the computer and the Task reports the result instead of this message.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages that computer's Gateway. Update it only through Check for updates; don't copy Gateway program files over by hand.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The selected Gateway route or client does not support the requested operation or form: privileged execution/streaming returned 404, a File request was rejected (400/404/405/422/501), terminal sessions are unsupported for this Gateway profile or cmd.exe, the client lacks captured execution, monitors lack terminal sessions, or an outbound path is unsupported.

What this means

  • The selected route or client lacks a required terminal or captured-execution method, rejects an unsupported outbound path, or returns a documented File or privilege endpoint rejection. Some File statuses can also mean an invalid request. The retained phase, target and receipt determine what executed. Rendering this definition adds no probe, retries, dispatch or changes to resource ownership.

Why this can happen

  • The selected route or client lacks a required terminal or captured-execution method, rejects an unsupported outbound path, or returns a documented File or privilege endpoint rejection. Some File statuses can also mean an invalid request.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare the requested capability and shell family with advertised support and the retained endpoint status; do not infer a mandatory upgrade from every rejection.

How to fix it

  • Read the specific message in Technical details. For privileged or File rejections, compare Server and Gateway versions and update the Gateway through its supported update path (a 400/422 File rejection can also mean the request itself is invalid). Terminal sessions need a POSIX or PowerShell shell profile: on Windows run the Linux Gateway inside WSL or use non-terminal execution (/exec, /exec/stream); cmd.exe terminals are unsupported.
  • Check capability and request compatibility. Correct a rejected payload or use a supported mode; update the intended Gateway only when the feature is unavailable.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended target advertises the operation and accepts a valid request with the required terminal or privilege support.

What not to do

  • Do not overwrite the original state with an incompatible version; use the supported upgrade path.

Technical notes

  • The retained phase, target and receipt determine what executed. Rendering this definition adds no probe, retries, dispatch or changes to resource ownership.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
